title: Partial-streaming parameter schema and failure transformation playbook
creator: Asha Morgan
description: Design and implement a backward-compatible JSON schema variant and runtime glue for tool/function call parameters that supports partial streaming inputs, incremental validation, and deterministic failure transformation into user-facing error codes and telemetry. This ticket captures the authoring format, runtime validation strategy, recovery heuristics for partial streams, and mapping from low-level runtime faults to actionable diagnostics for SDKs and Console.
proposal_summary: Introduce a compact 'streamableParam' attribute in the tool parameter manifest. Each parameter may declare a streaming policy (required|optional|buffered) and a set of coercion layers (parse->normalize->validate). Validation happens incrementally as bytes arrive; errors are classified into three broad classes (soft, hard, truncated) with deterministic transformation to canonical error objects that SDKs can translate into HTTP/gRPC codes and human messages. Provide migration shims so older tool manifests remain valid and runtime chooses non-streaming validation for legacy tools.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts new manifest field 'streamableParam' and correctly chooses incremental vs. buffered validation based on policy.
SDKs receive stable canonical error objects with fields: code, param, position, suggestion, and telemetry_id for tracing.
All existing tool manifests (no streamableParam) continue to validate under the legacy code path with no behavioral change.
Automated unit tests cover soft vs hard vs truncated error classification and mapping to HTTP 400/422/503 as appropriate.
Load test shows <5% p99 latency regression for typical small-parameter calls when streaming is enabled; telemetry metrics added to monitor.
Console renders per-call diagnostic with error code and suggested remediation links when tool validation fails during canary rollout.
decision_rationale: We need a single authoring surface that lets authors opt into streaming semantics without forcing global changes. Incremental validation reduces peak memory usage for large parameters (uploads, long JSON sequences) and improves perceived latency for downstream consumers. To avoid developer confusion, errors are normalized into a small set of machine-friendly codes and clear human suggestions; this aids both SDK UX and automated rollouts (canaries evaluate degraded quality separately). Backwards compatibility is critical: unknown fields default to legacy behavior.
implementation_plan: Spec: finalize 'streamableParam' keys and allowed streamingPolicy values (required|optional|buffered).
Runtime: add parser hooks that emit partial-validate events and a commit/rollback contract when streams end or abort.
Schema library: extend JSON schema utility to expose incremental validators and coercion pipelines (trim, base64-decode, json-stream-accumulator).
SDKs: adopt canonical error shape and display position/suggestion in common SDK clients (python/js/go).
Migrations: runtime feature-flag default off; add compatibility shim to treat streamableParam as non-streaming when flag disabled.
Docs: write authoring guide + examples and add a Console error translation table linking codes to remediation docs.
test_plan: Unit tests for parser hooks covering well-formed streaming sequences and out-of-order/chunk-missing scenarios.
Property tests that mutate incoming byte boundaries to ensure validator determinism.
Integration tests where a streaming client sends interleaved small and large parameters, asserting telemetry events and final call success/failure.
Chaos test: interrupt stream mid-parameter and verify truncated error classification and customer-visible message.
Performance regression test against baseline for small payloads and for large streamed payloads (1MB, 10MB).
rollout_plan: Enable in 'dev' and run full CI with new tests.
Canary rollout: 2% of traffic on a single region with telemetry dashboards monitoring: validation_errors_total, truncated_errors, p99_latency_delta.
If canary passes for 72 hours with error_rate_delta < 0.5% and no customer complaints, expand to 25% then 100%.
Deprecation: after 3 months of stable usage, update manifest reference docs and provide migration notes for authors who want buffered->required semantics.
